summary.headline: HOEC Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% QoQ to INR147 crore and EBITDA doubled to INR46 crore, helped by one-off B-80 HPCL crude realisation.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 profitability recovered sharply, with revenue from operations up 25% QoQ and EBITDA more than doubling, driven by higher gas sales and INR57.79 crore of HPCL crude revenue from B-80 inventory. H1 revenue fell to INR265 crore from INR405 crore because H1 FY26 included a one-time INR258 crore HPCL sale. Management reiterated an operating target of 11,000 boe/d by mid-2027, with ~10,000 boe/d net targeted by June 2027 and 22,000 boe/d by FY28-29 and 30,000-32,000 boe/d after B-174. Operational issues persisted at B-80 (D2 at 93-94% water cut, HPCL quality dispute, workover rig delay of about 15 days) and PY-1 gas evacuation remains contingent on a take-or-pay contract.

segments.name: B-80 (Bombay High, offshore)
segments.commentary: Highest operating cost asset (offshore support vessels, SBM and tanker maintenance); management cites 30-40% margins on a company basis and $20-30 opex per boe. D2 well at 93-94% water cut; workovers on D1 and D2 target 1,000-1,500 bopd plus 5-7 mmscfd gas, with rig arriving end-Nov/early Dec. 3 new wells to follow, drilling to finish by mid-May 2027.

segments.name: Dirok (Assam)
segments.commentary: Gross gas rate has risen to about 0.7 mmscmd from 0.4-0.5 mmscmd last quarter; capacity 1.2 mmscmd gross, with a further 2 mmscmd potential once evacuation is debottlenecked. Gas realisation about USD7.8-8/MMBTU in Q2 at PPAC price, currently around USD12/MMBTU.

segments.name: Kharsang (Assam)
segments.commentary: Oil production doubled; approval for 9 more wells, drilling to restart Jan-Feb 2027. Current gross oil about 680-700 bopd, targeted 1,200-1,400 bopd. Two gas-potential wells (8-9 mmscfd) remain shut in pending a 24 km pipeline to the Assam network.

segments.name: PY-1 (Cauvery Basin)
segments.commentary: Production was low and remains so; coil tubing intervention with SLB delayed by mobilisation issues. Management cites a PetroVietnam assessment of 15-20 mmscfd potential; new wells (USD20-25 million) will only be drilled after a firm take-or-pay contract with IOCL or GAIL.

segments.name: Cambay (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Palej production doubled; Asjol needs 2 wells; North Balol to add sucker rod pumps. Teaming up with GSPC and seeking third-party EOR partners.

guidance_outlook: Net HOEC production target of about 10,000 boe/d by June 2027 (range 8,500-11,000); earlier operating target of 11,000 boe/d by mid-2027 reiterated.
About 22,000 boe/d by end FY28 (after B-15 on stream ~June 2028, adding 3,000-3,500 boe/d) and 30,000-32,000 boe/d net by FY29 after B-174.
PY-1 expected to reach about 15 mmscfd (1,500-2,000 boe/d) by Dec 2027-Jan 2028 subject to contracts.
Dirok gas evacuation via DNPL line upgrade expected to be completed by end-Dec 2026 or mid-Dec; post-upgrade capacity 2.5 mmscmd at 90 bar.
B-80 workovers to be on stream by end-Dec/early Jan; 15-day delay expected to hit Q4 FY27 volumes. B-80 drilling from Oct 2027, on stream June 2028.

Funding: INR125 crore loan raised for workovers; bank facility of INR600-700 crore being pursued (total up to INR1,000 crore); about INR250 crore expected from liquidating HPCL crude and FSO B-80 crude.
capex_capacity: B-80: 2 workovers (D1, D2) plus 3 new wells; capex cited as USD45 million for wells and USD15 million for workover (USD60 million total, per management; an investor cited USD65 million). Rig demobilisation by 15 May for monsoon.

Dirok: DNPL pipeline spur and NRL bypass line under construction; DNPL material delivered; North Dirok drilling planned Jan-Feb 2027; B-19 exploration block (127-130 Bcf gross gas) expected to start mid-2027, subject to compensation dispute resolution.
Kharsang: 9 approved wells to start Jan-Feb 2027; 2 deep wells planned for Q3 2027.
B-174 (awarded 2026, DGH 2P 21 million boe): 8 locations, 5-6 material discoveries; drilling from Oct 2028 over about two years; new facilities planned.
Palej Part-2 (R2) PSC expected to be in place by January 2027 per management.
demand_pricing: Assam gas: PPAC-linked price around USD7.8/MMBTU in August, rising to about USD12/MMBTU for the current month; management hopes for USD9-11 average post NRL/national grid linkage.
Assam Gas Company takes about 20% of Dirok gas and is price sensitive; management expects a 10-20% volume impact once gas can be sold on national grid.
Dirok gas volumes stepped up to about 22 mmscfd in the quarter from about 14-15 mmscfd in prior quarters; management said this run-rate should hold.
Macro: IEA projects 2026 global oil demand down 2.6 mb/d; Asian spot LNG averaged about USD21.5/MMBTU March-October; India crude import bill up 46% to USD91 billion in H1.
Domestic crude and condensate production fell about 3.5% to 13.7 million tonnes; domestic gas production fell 4.4%.

qa_highlights.question: Asked for EBITDA and PAT margin ranges across Dirok, Kharsang, PY-1 and B-80 at about $70 crude.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined precise EBITDA guidance. B-80 margins are cited at 30-40% on a regular basis, with operating cost of $20-30/boe on a company basis; each $10/bbl oil price rise adds roughly INR30-40 crore revenue. Other assets were not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How should monsoon disruption risk at B-80 be viewed, and has the team learnt from past years?
qa_highlights.answer: Drilling will finish by 15 May when the rig demobilises. A small MOPU buffer gives 2-3 days of storage, and D1 kept producing through this monsoon. Subsea and SPM design is being reviewed for next year.

qa_highlights.question: Requested the net volume guidance for H2 FY27 and FY28, gross versus net.
qa_highlights.answer: About 10,000 boe/d net HOEC by June 2027 (range 8,500-11,000), 22,000 boe/d by FY28-end after B-15 (3,000-3,500 boe/d, on stream June 2028), and 30,000-32,000 boe/d by FY29 after B-174.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Dirok gas volumes rise to about 22 mmscfd from 14-15 mmscfd, and will this hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the run-rate should hold. Assam Gas Company (about 20% of Dirok gas) is price sensitive, and a 10-20% volume impact is expected once gas can be sold on the national grid. Gas realisation was about USD7.8-8/MMBTU in Q2, currently about USD12.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the DNPL line upgrade and grid connectivity timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The hot-tap option was dropped in favour of an NRL bypass line and spur line; material was delivered. Completion is targeted by end-December 2026, or mid-December at best, taking DNPL capacity from 1.2 to 2.5 mmscmd at 90 bar.

qa_highlights.question: What is the likelihood of PY-1 drilling next year, and what gates it?
qa_highlights.answer: No contracts will be awarded before a firm take-or-pay with IOCL or GAIL. Management gave a P50 chance of signing next year. Rented compressors are needed to lift pressure from 10 to 63 bar at the IOCL station about 24 km away.

risks_watch: B-80 workover rig arrives end-November/early December, so a 15-day delay is expected to hit Q4 FY27 volumes. Workovers target 1,000-1,500 bopd plus 5-7 mmscfd.

HPCL crude quality dispute and arbitration: about 36,104 MT of B-80 inventory remains to be monetised; about 120,000-130,000 bbl sits in the FSO. Dry-docking timing is January-March 2027, subject to tanker availability.
Dirok evacuation depends on the DNPL upgrade by December 2026 and national grid linkage. Price sensitivity of Assam Gas Company could cut volumes by 10-20%.
PY-1 drilling is conditional on a firm take-or-pay contract and rented compressors, which the board must approve. Funding routes include project-level partners and possible PY-1 equity dilution.

Funding: INR125 crore loan drawn; a bank facility of INR600-700 crore is being pursued; about INR250 crore is expected from liquidating HPCL and FSO crude. Peak capex falls in the next 3-4 months. Net debt/EBITDA is 0.71x.

Monsoon reliability at B-80: drilling stops 15 May; SPM and subsea design changes are planned for next year. Volume targets of 10,000 boe/d by June 2027 depend on these wells and on Kharsang and Cambay drilling.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the long-term volume path (10,000 boe/d by June 2027, 30,000-32,000 boe/d by FY29) and on the Dirok and B-80 recovery. It was cautious and non-committal on margins and EBITDA, on PY-1 drilling (gated by a take-or-pay contract) and on the exact timing of the DNPL upgrade. Some answers were deferred to follow-up discussions.
